gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Techtest.org (Michael Barton) measured the INIU Carry 20,000 mAh 45 W (P51L-E2) throttling to about 27 W under sustained load, and to 17 W when charging a laptop. ChatGPT picked this $36.99 bank as having 'enough output for the Deck'. The Phawx measured the Steam Deck OLED drawing 24 W in Cyberpunk 2077, so that leaves almost nothing to charge the Deck while playing. Also missing from every result: Techtest's measured delivered Wh for the main candidates, which runs from about 58 to 90 Wh.
standout_why: I opened gamingonbatteries.com/best-power-bank-steam-deck (the page titled 'Compared for Real Playtime'), vgkami.com (cited) and itechguides.com (cited). All three use only spec or listing numbers. Gamingonbatteries says its playtime table is 'calculated estimates… not lab-measured results'. Vgkami says its figures 'are not results from independent hands-on testing'. Itechguides says the specs 'do not establish' a tested winner. None gives a measured delivered Wh, a throttling result or a measured Deck power draw for any named bank. ChatGPT's own answers call their runtime tables 'rough estimates, not measured benchmarks'.
decides: It knocks out the INIU Carry 45 W (P51L-E2) as a pick for charging while playing. Its 45 W rating does not hold: Techtest measured it throttling to about 27 W from heat, close to the Deck OLED's measured 24 W draw. It also ranks the bigger banks by measured energy rather than mAh. Anker Prime 26K 300 W delivered 79.6–89.8 Wh. Anker 737 averaged 74.6 Wh, peaking at 78.0 Wh at 20 V/3 A. Anker A1695 averaged 74.2 Wh. UGREEN 25K 165 W (PB552) averaged 72.6 Wh. UGREEN 20K 165 W retractable (PB726) delivered 62.5–66.4 Wh. UGREEN 20K 130 W delivered only 54.8–64.7 Wh, falling as load rose. So the 25 K-class banks give about 10 Wh more usable energy than the 20 K UGREENs, roughly 25 extra minutes at 24 W. The UGREEN 25K 165 W gives about the same measured energy as the Anker A1695 and is listed for less. One limit: Techtest found the UGREEN PB552 throttled from 140 W to 65 W at about half charge, but 65 W is still above the Deck's 45 W.

That is the bank ChatGPT recommended.
